article_context: 文章分析美国“小费扩张”和“小费通胀”：数字支付让商家更容易在服务前索要更高小费，虽然这能补充低薪服务人员收入，却也让小费越来越带有强迫意味，并与服务质量脱节。

article.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 数字支付正在把小费推向更多场景
article.background: 文章分析美国“小费扩张”和“小费通胀”：数字支付让商家更容易在服务前索要更高小费，虽然这能补充低薪服务人员收入，却也让小费越来越带有强迫意味，并与服务质量脱节。

sentences.en: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
sentences.zh: 历史上，美国顾客通常给那些被认为主要靠小费维持收入的人付小费，比如工资低于最低工资标准的餐厅服务员。

segments.text: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.

sentences.en: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
sentences.zh: 2010年代初，各类商家开始使用 iPad 和其他数字支付系统处理消费付款。

segments.text: In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.

sentences.en: These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
sentences.zh: 这些系统常常提示顾客为过去并不需要给小费的服务支付小费。

segments.text: These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.

sentences.en: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
sentences.zh: 如今的小费请求往往已经与过去决定人们何时、如何给小费的薪酬和服务规范脱离。

segments.text: Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.

sentences.en: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
sentences.zh: 过去，顾客几乎总是在服务完成后才付小费，例如用完餐、剪完头发或披萨送到之后。

segments.text: Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.

sentences.en: That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
sentences.zh: 这种支付时点可以奖励优质服务，也能激励工作人员提供更好的服务。

segments.text: That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.

sentences.en: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
sentences.zh: 如今，服务开始之前就要求付小费的情况越来越常见。

segments.text: It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.

sentences.en: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
sentences.zh: 新的小费支付技术甚至可能自动把小费加到账单里。

segments.text: And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.

sentences.en: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.
sentences.zh: 数字支付设备的普及，让商家更容易向顾客索要小费。

segments.text: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.

sentences.en: That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.
sentences.zh: 这在一定程度上解释了为什么小费请求正逐渐进入新的服务领域。

segments.text: That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.

sentences.en: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.
sentences.zh: 顾客如今经常会看到一列默认建议小费选项，其中往往有远高于应付金额20%的比例。

segments.text: Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.

sentences.en: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
sentences.zh: 小费比例从20世纪50年代的10%或更低，上升到2000年前后的15%，再到如今的20%甚至更高。

segments.text: The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.

sentences.en: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
sentences.zh: 这种增长有时被称为“小费通胀”，即人们被期待支付越来越高的小费。

segments.text: This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.

sentences.en: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.
sentences.zh: 对餐厅等历来依赖小费的服务行业员工而言，小费一直是重要收入来源；这类岗位的法定小费最低工资可能低至每小时2.13美元。

segments.text: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.

sentences.en: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
sentences.zh: 如今，小费适用范围扩大和“小费通胀”又进一步补充了许多低薪服务人员的收入。

segments.text: Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.

sentences.en: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
sentences.zh: 值得注意的是，小费主要让其中一部分员工受益，例如服务员，却未必惠及厨师和洗碗工等其他员工。

segments.text: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.

sentences.en: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
sentences.zh: 为了确保所有员工获得公平工资，一些餐厅曾取消小费并提高价格，但这种转向无小费服务的运动如今基本已经偃旗息鼓。

segments.text: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.

sentences.en: So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了在不涨价的情况下提高员工工资，越来越多雇主正屈从于扩大小费范围和提高小费比例的诱惑。

segments.text: So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.

sentences.en: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often.
sentences.zh: 然而，许多顾客感到不满，因为他们觉得自己被过于频繁地要求支付过高的小费。

segments.text: However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often.

sentences.en: And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.
sentences.zh: 正如我们的研究所强调的，如今的小费似乎更具强迫性、更少体现慷慨，而且常常与服务质量完全脱节。

segments.text: And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.
